flawed_step: Lines 5–13 differentiate an O(z^{-1}) remainder and assert its derivative is O(z^{-1}); this does not follow from a big-O bound.
counterexample: For real x>1, let R(x)=sin(x^2)/x. Then |R(x)|≤1/x, so R(x)=O(x^{-1}). But R'(x)=2cos(x^2)-sin(x^2)/x^2. At x_n=sqrt(2πn), R'(x_n)=2. Hence R' is not O(x^{-1}), since 2≤C/x_n cannot hold for all n.
assessment_summary: The proof relies on an invalid general rule for differentiating big-O terms. Additional analytic estimates would be needed to control the derivative of the particular Stirling remainder.
